question: Two friends compared their savings for a trip. Noor had 39 dollars saved, even though the trip costs 500 dollars for the whole group. She earned 24 more dollars from a garage sale. She then split her savings evenly among 3 jars for different goals and kept only the travel jar going forward. Three more matching deposits made that jar four times as large. Finally, she split that jar evenly among 3 more expenses and kept only the plane ticket portion, ending up with less than her friend Dahlia. How much money did Noor have in the plane ticket portion?

A coordinator had 116 tasks initially. She removed 109. This was multiplied by 3. Then multiplied by 4. Then multiplied by 3. Then multiplied by 2 for a full calculation. What was the final project scope?

A concert venue starts ticket sales with 105 tickets already reserved for VIP guests. A presale event brings that number to 7 times what it was. A general sale then brings the reserved count to 8 times what it had grown to. A processing error causes 5,128 of those tickets to be released back into general inventory by mistake. The remaining reserved tickets are then split evenly between the venue's two VIP entrances, and the story follows just one entrance's list. Finally, 64 names are removed from that entrance's list after a late round of cancellations that took 55 minutes, just under an hour, to fully process. How many names remain on that one entrance's list?

Amina prints more wallpaper than her partner Gustav does. She started with 163 rolls, and each roll was cut into 7 lengths. A shop bought 512 lengths. The mill then printed 9 lengths for every length she had left. A hotel contract took 2415 lengths, and a chain store finally ordered 8 lengths for every length remaining. The mill has 24 printing tables. How many lengths does the chain store's order come to?

A gym instructor taught 45 classes last month, and each class began with 7 minutes of warm-up. Across the month she also spent 40 minutes on stretching demonstrations. Cooling the classes down took a further 46 minutes in total, and she logged 39 minutes of paperwork. Her timesheet is kept in minutes rather than in hours. How many minutes did the instructor log for the month?

A library had 163 books on its main shelf. During the morning, 23 books were returned. By afternoon, 39 more books were returned. Then, 201 books were removed for repair. The remaining books were reduced to a third. Finally, 26 new books were added. The library received a donation of 50 books. How many books does the library have at the end?

Petra grows more pumpkins than her brother Lukas does. She brought 240 pumpkins to the autumn market, and the stallholder cut each one into 7 wedges. During the day 106 wedges were sold. Lukas contributed 38 wedges from his own crop, and a neighbour added 78 more. The market runs for 12 hours. How many wedges are on the stall at the end?

The juice stand had 239 gallons of juice, recorded in quarts at 4 quarts to a gallon. A delivery added 30 quarts, and 535 quarts were sold. The owner then doubled the remaining stock by pressing the same amount again. Juice is served in cups, at 4 cups to a quart. How many cups can the stand serve?

In the morning Kofi arrived at the fun fair with 50 vouchers and was given 20 more at the gate. He exchanged every voucher for 4 game tokens. In the afternoon the games switched to plastic chips, so he swapped every token for 2 chips, and then won 12 more chips at the hoopla. The fair had 9 rides in all. In the evening he lost 423 chips at the shooting gallery, and at closing time the cashier paid him 7 cents for every chip he handed in. How many cents did Kofi receive?

Dario belongs to a coffee shop rewards program and has been a member for half a year. He earned 170 points in each of the last 7 weeks. The shop, which has 3 locations in town, gave him a 48-point birthday bonus. A survey he filled out added another 13 points. He then redeemed 1200 points for a coffee grinder. How many points does Dario have left in his account?
A manager started 94 items. Added 75. Removed 54. Added 21. Multiplied by 5. Lost 529 returns. What is final?

Two siblings, Owen and Kira, compared their saved allowance, and Kira's stash was noticeably smaller than his. Owen started with 24 dollars saved. He earned 51 more dollars doing chores. He then earned 70 more dollars from a birthday gift. His savings were split evenly across 5 jars, and only one jar was tracked going forward. That jar then lost 13 dollars when he bought a video game. A bonus from grandma made that jar's total grow to 8 times its size. How much money was in that jar?

A farmer had 171 eggs to sell at the market. He used 120 eggs to make pasta. He then multiplied his remaining product quantity by 4, and then by 8. His production multiplied by 9 to meet demand. He split his shipment equally between 2 distribution centers. Then he split each center's share in half again. How many units did each final location receive?

A farm had 36 eggs initially. They multiplied by 5 for collection. They added 69 from the morning. They multiplied by 8 for storage crates. They multiplied by 2 for both henhouses. They divided by 2 for equal distribution. They added 78 from afternoon laying. The farm had 10 chickens. How many eggs distributed?

A beekeeper filled 180 jars with honey during the summer. 140 of the jars were sold at the farmers' market. A neighbour returned 3 jars that had not been opened, and half of her jars carry a blue label. In the autumn 34 jars were given away as gifts and 4 were dropped and broken. She now plans 7 hives, each producing as many jars as she has left. A friend then gave her 4 filled jars from his own hive. How many jars of honey will she have?

A store had 137 items. They multiplied by 5 for sales projection. They subtracted 256 items sold. They subtracted 376 items in process. They subtracted 5 items for quality removal. They doubled the remainder. Finally, they divided by 4 for four-location distribution. Using one distractor and minutes-to-hours conversion, how many items per location?

A shipping company tracked the total number of packages in Container A all week, starting with 216 packages. A supplier's shipment tripled the tracked package count. A regional hub then multiplied the tracked count by 6. A holiday surge multiplied it by 9 more. Converting the tracked count from packages to a weight estimate in kilograms for customs — a simple unit change — the company then subtracted 34821 units after a customs adjustment. A dozen customs agents processed the shipment, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked count. How many units did the tracked customs total show?
A bakery had 63 loaves morning. Divided by 3 for equal shops. Added 4. Added 68 afternoon shipment. Multiplied by 6 evening distribution. What was evening total?

A summer camp owns 138 tents, but 15 of them were torn in a storm and taken out of service. Every tent that is still usable sleeps 2 campers. A further 74 campers are staying in the wooden cabins by the lake. Each camper at the site is issued 6 meal tickets for the week, and every meal ticket can be exchanged for 8 tokens at the canteen. The lake is 3 kilometres across at its widest point. How many tokens could the campers claim altogether?
In the morning, a warehouse had 236 items. They removed 83. By afternoon, they added 55. They multiplied by 8. They multiplied by 8. By evening, they removed 12702. How many items?

On Monday morning Tara had 45 jars of jam ready for the fair. She sold 25 of them at the early market. In the afternoon she made 68 more jars. Her sister Wendy had prepared exactly the same number of jars as Tara was holding by then, and the 2 sisters put all of their jars onto one stall. In the evening their father brought 18 extra jars to the stall. How many jars were on the stall that evening?

A community garden tracked the total number of pumpkins growing in its main patch throughout the season, starting with 237 pumpkins in early summer. By midsummer, a second patch's crop added 61 more pumpkins to the tracked total. By late summer, ideal weather multiplied the tracked pumpkin count by 7. By early fall, a final growth spurt added 29 more pumpkins. By mid-fall, a blight destroyed 236 pumpkins from the tracked patch. A separate community garden across town, unrelated to this patch, grew 500 pumpkins. By late fall, a final harvest added 22 more pumpkins to the tracked total. How many pumpkins did the tracked patch show by late fall?

Tomás tracked the total dollars in his arcade token jar, starting with 17 dollars worth of tokens. His cousin Nadia, by comparison, had a jar with a mere dozen dollars worth, but only Tomás's jar is tracked here. He spent 11 dollars worth of tokens on a claw machine. He spent another 5 dollars worth on skee-ball. A birthday bonus then multiplied his tracked token value by 6. Finally, a loyalty reward multiplied his tracked value by 5. How many dollars worth of tokens did Tomás's tracked jar hold after the loyalty reward?

A student started with 54 pages of notes. She divided in half to 27 pages for review. She multiplied by 8 times to 216 pages. She expanded 6 times to 1,296 pages. She doubled to 2,592 pages for comprehensive study. She added 47 pages of new material, reaching 2,639. She removed 1,856 outdated pages. How many current pages remain?

A product started with 97 units. In the morning, production multiplied by 8. By afternoon, output multiplied by 4 more. Then 53 units were added from a shipment. By evening, 3030 units were removed for distribution. The count was measured in bundles of items. How many units remained in storage?
